#9846. Pickle Juice Vs Buttermilk: Which Marinade Is Best For Fried Chicken?

When it comes to down-home Southern cooking, buttermilk and pickles both have a prominent place thanks to their flavors and how they affect the chemistry of cooking. Todd Johnson, Proprietor of Strips Chicken & Brewing, insists that both have a place in fried chicken — although he asserts that buttermilk is the better all-around choice.

"If you're going to marinate your chicken, buttermilk wins," Johnson told Food Republic. "It's gently acidic, so it softens the surface of the chicken without turning it mushy. It's also thick enough to leave a tacky layer that flour clings to. That's the foundation of a craggy, crunchy crust." Just about any marinade can infuse the muscle fibers with moisture and keep it more tender, but it's that combination of subtle acid, sugars, and milk solids that gives it a more well-rounded, heartier flavor and makes it such an essential ingredient in fried chicken. Since it lacks the potency of a pickle brine, it also tends to absorb other seasonings quite well, so you don't have to rely solely on your breading.

While Johnson admits to being "not a fan of pickle juice as a marinade," he noted that it can have its place. "It's already salty and acidic, so it seasons and moistens the meat quickly," he explained. "You'll notice results in a couple of hours instead of overnight." Still, its high acidity means you have a narrower window between tender and mushy chicken, so it's not an ideal choice for beginners. Brine is a pretty potent ingredient, so while it's effective, it also calls for an experienced hand unless you're willing to experiment.

Good fried chicken has three components: meat, breading, and oil. Buttermilk is such a mainstay in recipes because it has a delicious effect on all three of these, promoting flavor, browning, and texture.

One of many major mistakes everyone makes with fried chicken is creating a breading that doesn't stick, and dry ingredients aren't the only contributor to this. "Oil and fat act like a release agent between meat and crust," Todd Johnson explained. "That's why we use fat-free buttermilk." For this aspect, it may seem like pickle brine is the right choice, but Johnson said that its lack of fat comes at the cost of a thinner consistency. Fat-free buttermilk is far more adhesive, giving your dry ingredients a prime surface to cling to, so they won't fall off the meat once they hit the oil.

Johnson conceded that buttermilk has a tendency to "over-brown" if your oil gets too hot, burning the milk sugars and solids, fouling the flavor. This is a pretty hefty disadvantage, but one that can be turned to an advantage with a careful eye. If you maintain Johnson's recommended oil temperature of 350 degrees Fahrenheit, you can toast, rather than burn, those solids, delivering a robust flavor profile focused on a hearty, umami-rich breading. Buttermilk is also a more convenient option, as you can just remove the excess drippings and drop your meat directly into your breading.

When you're looking to make fried chicken on the fly or don't have a surplus of seasoning, there are few options better than pickle brine. Todd Johnson said it's indispensable for achieving that "sandwich shop flavor" that some folks prefer, even if it has its quirks.

While you can always add some salt to your buttermilk, it won't have quite the same effect as using a jar of leftover pickle brine. "It's already salty and acidic, so it seasons and moistens the meat quickly," Todd Johnson clarified. Its extremely high and well-dissolved sodium content loosens up muscle fibers, making them far better at retaining moisture. While it lacks the rich solids and sugars of buttermilk, it brings far more tang, so it'll cut through even the heartiest, most marbled pieces of fried meat quite easily.

The biggest downside to pickle juice in your marinade is inconsistency and lack of other seasoning options. Not all brines are made the same, so unless you work with the exact same brand and product every time, there's always some amount of guess work involved. While pickle juice is one of the most powerful vehicles for flavor, it also leaves very little room for anything more subtle or nuanced. After marinating your meat, you'll also need to carefully pat dry each piece before tossing it in a batter or dry ingredients. Excess surface moisture creates a steam barrier between your chicken and breading, so even a bit left on the surface can ruin your food.

#9841. Skip Expensive Sea Bass: The Cheaper Fish Alternative With More Omega-3

It's never a bad idea to get more seafood into your diet. It's a great source of protein, loaded with a whole alphabet of nutrients, and most importantly, it's reliably delicious. There's an endless variety of seafood to suit any taste, and one fish many shoppers reach for is Chilean sea bass; however, anyone familiar with it knows it rarely comes cheap. If you're in the market for something rich and buttery without the sky-high price, sablefish is an excellent alternative.

Sablefish, commonly known as black cod, is a deep-water fish native to the North Pacific, ranging from Mexico to Alaska and the Bering Sea. Despite the name, it isn't a true cod, just as Chilean sea bass isn't a true bass. Both are white fish, a category usually associated with lean flesh, but these two are the exception to the rule. Because they live in cold, deep waters, they store plenty of omega-3-rich fat. But that doesn't make them equal. In fact, sablefish outranks not only sea bass but virtually any other whitefish when it comes to omega-3 content.

Its famously high fat content gives sablefish its indulgently rich, buttery texture and juicy flavor. For reference, salmon is the fish most people associate with omega-3s, and sablefish lands in the same ballpark with practically the same amounts (per Oregon State University). Surprisingly, despite being the richer option of the two whitefish, it tends to come in considerably cheaper than pricey Chilean sea bass, with strong catches and population booms strongly contributing to its more approachable price point.

Though sablefish is generally more affordable than Chilean sea bass, that doesn't necessarily mean it's budget-friendly. It remains a favorite at high-end restaurants, and one of the most famous examples is Nobu. At this Japanese-Peruvian fusion spot beloved by celebrities, miso-marinated black cod is one of its signature dishes. Fortunately, you can recreate this viral favorite at home without paying an arm or a leg.

Simply leave the fillets in a mixture of miso paste, mirin, sake, and sugar for at least two hours, or ideally overnight, to let the flavors work their way into the fish. When you're ready to cook, scrape off the excess marinade and broil the fish for around seven minutes, until the surface is beautifully caramelized and lightly charred while the inside remains tender and buttery. Pair that with some sushi rice made Chef Nobu style for a Michelin-worthy dinner all from the comfort of your own home.

When it comes to cooking, sablefish sets itself apart from the cod it shares its name with thanks to its high fat content. Your standard Atlantic or Pacific cod is exceptionally lean, making it protein-dense but also a little trickier to cook without drying out. Black cod, meanwhile, is far more forgiving when it comes to heat. Its generous fat content helps protect the flesh from drying out, even when exposed to high temperatures, making it an excellent candidate for a wide range of cooking methods, from pan-searing and grilling to broiling, roasting, pan-frying, and even smoking.

#9838. Federated AI Still Has a Central Coordinator Problem

Here's the problem federated learning is trying to solve: Most AI training starts with pooling data. That fails wherever the data is sensitive or legally stuck. In 2023, Samsung reportedly restricted employee use of ChatGPT after engineers pasted internal source code into it. In late 2024, Italy’s data protection authority fined OpenAI €15M over how personal data was handled in training. Hospitals hold exactly the data that could improve diagnostic models, but they can’t simply merge patient records.

Federated learning is the standard answer: instead of moving data to the model, move the model to the data. Each site trains locally and sends only model updates to a coordinator, which aggregates them. It’s not theoretical. Google has used it for on-device keyboard prediction in Gboard, and a multi-hospital study (EXAM) trained a COVID-19 oxygen-needs model across roughly 20 institutions without sharing patient records.

“The data never leaves” is not the same as “nothing leaks.” Model updates are computed from private data, and researchers have shown that training examples can sometimes be reconstructed from shared gradients (see Deep Leakage from Gradients, Zhu et al., 2019). Membership inference attacks can also reveal whether a specific record was in the training set.

Both help. Neither is free. Any claim of “private AI” should come with the accuracy cost attached.

This is the part the marketing skips. In most federated systems, one party runs the coordinator, owns the global model, and decides who participates. The data is distributed, but control isn’t. That’s centralized AI with extra steps.

If the goal is the open, user-owned AI that this contest is about, federation alone doesn’t deliver it. You also need verifiable records of what happened, independent compute, and governance people can contest.

None of this is hypothetical. Each layer has open-source tooling today:

Almost all federated learning is about prediction: classify this image, predict the next word. But decisions in medicine and policy depend on causal questions: does this treatment help, or do sicker patients just receive it more often?

Learning causal structure across silos is harder. Sites may measure different variables, confounders differ from site to site, and local graphs may disagree. Federated causal discovery work exists, but it’s far less mature than federated prediction. A practical starting point is to learn a causal graph locally at each site (for example with pgmpy), merge the graphs in an aggregation step, and test whether the merged structure stays consistent across sites.

A hospital in Delhi, one in Nairobi and one in São Paulo improve a shared model without any patient record leaving the building. The coordinator is a protocol anyone can audit. Every training round leaves a verifiable record of which sources, configuration and model version produced the result. Contributors are rewarded for useful updates instead of having their data harvested for free.

#9835. Ahrefs vs SEMrush: Which SEO Tool Should You Use?


SEMrush and Ahrefs are among the most popular tools in the SEO industry. Both companies have been in business for years and have thousands of customers per month.

If you're a professional SEO or trying to do digital marketing on your own, at some point you'll likely consider using a tool to help with your efforts. Ahrefs and SEMrush are two names that will likely appear on your shortlist.

In this guide, I'm going to help you learn more about these SEO tools and how to choose the one that's best for your purposes.

What is SEMrush?


SEMrush is a popular SEO tool with a wide range of features—it's the leading competitor research service for online marketers. SEMrush's SEO Keyword Magic tool offers over 20 billion Google-approved keywords, which are constantly updated and it's the largest keyword database.

The program was developed in 2007 as SeoQuake is a small Firefox extension

Features

  • Most accurate keyword data: Accurate keyword search volume data is crucial for SEO and PPC campaigns by allowing you to identify what keywords are most likely to bring in big sales from ad clicks. SEMrush constantly updates its databases and provides the most accurate data.
  • Largest Keyword database: SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool now features 20-billion keywords, providing marketers and SEO professionals the largest database of keywords.

  • All SEMrush users receive daily ranking data, mobile volume information, and the option to buy additional keywords by default with no additional payment or add-ons needed
  • Most accurate position tracking tool: This tool provides all subscribers with basic tracking capabilities, making it suitable for SEO professionals. Plus, the Position Tracking tool provides local-level data to everyone who uses the tool.
  • SEO Data Management: SEMrush makes managing your online data easy by allowing you to create visually appealing custom PDF reports, including Branded and White Label reports, report scheduling, and integration with GA, GMB, and GSC.
  • Toxic link monitoring and penalty recovery: With SEMrush, you can make a detailed analysis of toxic backlinks, toxic scores, toxic markers, and outreach to those sites.
  • Content Optimization and Creation Tools: SEMrush offers content optimization and creation tools that let you create SEO-friendly content. Some features include the SEO Writing Assistant, On-Page SEO Check, er/SEO Content Template, Content Audit, Post Tracking, Brand Monitoring.

Ahrefs



Ahrefs is a leading SEO platform that offers a set of tools to grow your search traffic, research your competitors, and monitor your niche. The company was founded in 2010, and it has become a popular choice among SEO tools. Ahrefs has a keyword index of over 10.3 billion keywords and offers accurate and extensive backlink data updated every 15-30 minutes and it is the world's most extensive backlink index database.

Features

  • Backlink alerts data and new keywords: Get an alert when your site is linked to or discussed in blogs, forums, comments, or when new keywords are added to a blog posting about you.
  • Intuitive interface: The intuitive design of the widget helps you see the overall health of your website and search engine ranking at a glance.
  • Site Explorer: The Site Explorer will give you an in-depth look at your site's search traffic.
  • Domain Comparison
  • Reports with charts and graphs
  • JavaScript rendering and a site audit can identify SEO issues.
  • A question explorer that provides well-crafted topic suggestions

Direct Comparisons: Ahrefs vs SEMrush

Now that you know a little more about each tool, let's take a look at how they compare. I'll analyze each tool to see how they differ in interfaces, keyword research resources, rank tracking, and competitor analysis.

User Interface

Ahrefs and SEMrush both offer comprehensive information and quick metrics regarding your website's SEO performance. However, Ahrefs takes a bit more of a hands-on approach to getting your account fully set up, whereas SEMrush's simpler dashboard can give you access to the data you need quickly.

In this section, we provide a brief overview of the elements found on each dashboard and highlight the ease with which you can complete tasks.

AHREFS



The Ahrefs dashboard is less cluttered than that of SEMrush, and its primary menu is at the very top of the page, with a search bar designed only for entering URLs.

Additional features of the Ahrefs platform include:

  • You can see analytics from the dashboard, including search engine rankings to domain ratings, referring domains, and backlink
  • Jumping from one tool to another is easy. You can use the Keyword Explorer to find a keyword to target and then directly track your ranking with one click.
  • The website offers a tooltip helper tool that allows you to hover your mouse over something that isn't clear and get an in-depth explanation.

SEMRUSH



When you log into the SEMrush Tool, you will find four main modules. These include information about your domains, organic keyword analysis, ad keyword, and site traffic.

You'll also find some other options like

  • A search bar allows you to enter a domain, keyword, or anything else you wish to explore.
  • A menu on the left side of the page provides quick links to relevant information, including marketing insights, projects, keyword analytics, and more.
  • The customer support resources located directly within the dashboard can be used to communicate with the support team or to learn about other resources such as webinars and blogs.
  • Detailed descriptions of every resource offered. This detail is beneficial for new marketers, who are just starting.

WHO WINS?

Both Ahrefs and SEMrush have user-friendly dashboards, but Ahrefs is less cluttered and easier to navigate. On the other hand, SEMrush offers dozens of extra tools, including access to customer support resources.

When deciding on which dashboard to use, consider what you value in the user interface, and test out both.

Rank Tracking

If you're looking to track your website's search engine ranking, rank tracking features can help. You can also use them to monitor your competitors.

Let's take a look at Ahrefs vs. SEMrush to see which tool does a better job.

Ahrefs



The Ahrefs Rank Tracker is simpler to use. Just type in the domain name and keywords you want to analyze, and it spits out a report showing you the search engine results page (SERP) ranking for each keyword you enter.

Rank Tracker looks at the ranking performance of keywords and compares them with the top rankings for those keywords. Ahrefs also offers:

You'll see metrics that help you understand your visibility, traffic, average position, and keyword difficulty.

It gives you an idea of whether a keyword would be profitable to target or not.

SEMRUSH



SEMRush offers a tool called Position Tracking. This tool is a project tool—you must set it up as a new project. Below are a few of the most popular features of the SEMrush Position Tracking tool:

All subscribers are given regular data updates and mobile search rankings upon subscribing

The platform provides opportunities to track several SERP features, including Local tracking.

Intuitive reports allow you to track statistics for the pages on your website, as well as the keywords used in those pages.

Identify pages that may be competing with each other using the Cannibalization report.

WHO WINS?

Ahrefs is a more user-friendly option. It takes seconds to enter a domain name and keywords. From there, you can quickly decide whether to proceed with that keyword or figure out how to rank better for other keywords.

SEMrush allows you to check your mobile rankings and ranking updates daily, which is something Ahrefs does not offer. SEMrush also offers social media rankings, a tool you won't find within the Ahrefs platform. Both are good which one do you like let me know in the comment.

Keyword Research

Keyword research is closely related to rank tracking, but it's used for deciding which keywords you plan on using for future content rather than those you use now.

When it comes to SEO, keyword research is the most important thing to consider when comparing the two platforms.

AHREFS



The Ahrefs Keyword Explorer provides you with thousands of keyword ideas and filters search results based on the chosen search engine.

Ahrefs supports several features, including:

  • It can search multiple keywords in a single search and analyze them together. At SEMrush, you also have this feature in Keyword Overview.
  • Ahrefs has a variety of keywords for different search engines, including Google, YouTube, Amazon, Bing, Yahoo, Yandex, and other search engines.
  • When you click on a keyword, you can see its search volume and keyword difficulty, but also other keywords related to it, which you didn't use.

SEMRUSH



SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool has over 20 billion keywords for Google. You can type in any keyword you want, and a list of suggested keywords will appear.

The Keyword Magic Tool also lets you to:

  • Show performance metrics by keyword
  • Search results are based on both broad and exact keyword matches.
  • Show data like search volume, trends, keyword difficulty, and CPC.
  • Show the first 100 Google search results for any keyword.
  • Identify SERP Features and Questions related to each keyword
  • SEMrush has released a new Keyword Gap Tool that uncovers potentially useful keyword opportunities for you, including both paid and organic keywords.

WHO WINS?

Both of these tools offer keyword research features and allow users to break down complicated tasks into something that can be understood by beginners and advanced users alike.

If you're interested in keyword suggestions, SEMrush appears to have more keyword suggestions than Ahrefs does. It also continues to add new features, like the Keyword Gap tool and SERP Questions recommendations.

Competitor Analysis

Both platforms offer competitor analysis tools, eliminating the need to come up with keywords off the top of your head. Each tool is useful for finding keywords that will be useful for your competition so you know they will be valuable to you.

AHREFS



Ahrefs' domain comparison tool lets you compare up to five websites (your website and four competitors) side-by-side.it also shows you how your site is ranked against others with metrics such as backlinks, domain ratings, and more.

Use the Competing Domains section to see a list of your most direct competitors, and explore how many keywords matches your competitors have.

To find more information about your competitor, you can look at the Site Explorer and Content Explorer tools and type in their URL instead of yours.

SEMRUSH



SEMrush provides a variety of insights into your competitors' marketing tactics. The platform enables you to research your competitors effectively. It also offers several resources for competitor analysis including:

Traffic Analytics helps you identify where your audience comes from, how they engage with your site, what devices visitors use to view your site, and how your audiences overlap with other websites.

SEMrush's Organic Research examines your website's major competitors and shows their organic search rankings, keywords they are ranking for, and even if they are ranking for any (SERP) features and more.

The Market Explorer search field allows you to type in a domain and lists websites or articles similar to what you entered. Market Explorer also allows users to perform in-depth data analytics on These companies and markets.

WHO WINS?

SEMrush wins here because it has more tools dedicated to competitor analysis than Ahrefs. However, Ahrefs offers a lot of functionality in this area, too. It takes a combination of both tools to gain an advantage over your competition.

Pricing

Ahrefs

  • Lite Monthly: $99/month
  • Standard Monthly: $179/month
  • Annually Lite: $990/year
  • Annually Standard: $1790/year

SEMRUSH

  • Pro Plan: $119.95/month
  • Guru Plan:$229.95/month
  • Business Plan: $449.95/month

Which SEO tool should you choose for digital marketing?

When it comes to keyword data research, you will become confused about which one to choose.

Consider choosing Ahrefs if you

  • Like friendly and clean interface
  • Searching for simple keyword suggestions

  • Want to get more keywords for different search engines like Amazon, Bing, Yahoo, Yandex, Baidu, and more

 

Consider SEMrush if you:

  • Want more marketing and SEO features
  • Need competitor analysis tool
  • Need to keep your backlinks profile clean
  • Looking for more keyword suggestions for Google

Both tools are great. Choose the one which meets your requirements and if you have any experience using either Ahrefs or SEMrush let me know in the comment section which works well for you.

#9833. Turn Wendy's Chili Into Game Day Nacho Dip With This Ex-Employee's Simple Hack

Wendy's menu includes many items you might expect to find at a fast food joint: burgers (although it uniquely offers square patties), fries, chicken nuggets, and salads. But the chain is also a standout in the drive-thru world, as it's one of the few major brands to offer customers items like baked potatoes and bowls of chili, the latter of which are truly comforting after a long day when you want something hearty and filling. Wendy's chili can also be useful on game day as the base for a single-serve nacho dip, and all you have to do is add nacho cheese and sour cream.

The creator of this hack — a former Wendy's employee — simply adds the two extra ingredients and gives it a thorough stir, so it's an incredibly easy upgrade to pull off. Both the nacho cheese and the sour cream will mix easily into the chili, provided it's still hot, or at least warm, from the restaurant, with the cheese adding richness and the sour cream lending a welcome tang. Together, they also create a creamier consistency that makes it perfect for dipping.

If it has cooled, you might want to give it a quick nuke in the microwave (in a different vessel). If it's not quite nacho-y enough for your tastes, you can absolutely sprinkle in some smoky taco seasoning. Or dress it up with some diced jalapeños for heat, and top it with green onions to cut through all the richness.

If you head to your local Wendy's to pick up the ingredients for this nacho cheese dip hack, you might run into some confusion when ordering the cheese sauce, as some customers have reportedly had trouble purchasing it because employees couldn't figure out how to ring it up. Fortunately, several Redditors shared that the sauce can be found under Sides, then Cheese Menu, where it's listed as Cheese Sauce. With that information, you should be able to secure the goods (for a small fee), and the cashier will likely think you're a Wendy's whisperer.

Now, while you're ordering, it might occur to you to get something to dunk into your makeshift nacho dip. Fries are the obvious choice, and Wendy's spuds are particularly well-suited to the job, since they're slightly thicker-cut than some of their fast food counterparts, so they can stand up to the chunky chili better. In a pinch, the saltine crackers that come on the side make for a tasty way to scoop up the dip, but you'd be remiss if you didn't also consider the acclaimed spicy nuggets, or Wendy's Tendys, the chain's juicy breaded chicken strips.

This adorable cake pulls double duty, serving as both a scene-stealing centerpiece and a feast-ending dessert. To make, stack two mini Bundt cakes together and frost with orange buttercream. Carving this frosted pumpkin at the end of the meal may just upstage the turkey!

To make this recipe, you’ll need: Mini Bundt Pan Set

A combination of pie and pudding, the name comes from the method in which the recipe is completed: After an apple-based filling is baked in a crust-lined casserole, the baker takes a fork and "dowdies" the crust, breaking it into pieces that remain crisp despite being partially immersed in the juicy filling.

To make this recipe, you’ll need: 9" square pan

If you don’t want to fuss with pie, we suggest making a cobbler instead. This fruit-filled version pairs juicy spiced apples with a crackly brown sugar crust — both prep and serving are easy, and the resulting cobbler will absolutely steal the show.

Instead of slicing and serving dessert, bake every guest their own individual mini cake. Start with a moist, spicy sheet cake, then use a biscuit cutter or overturned glass to cut rounds for individual layer cakes sandwiched with cream cheese frosting.

#9828. Skip Salmon: 15 More Sustainable Fish Alternatives

From Japan to New Jersey, salmon is one of the most in-demand, beloved fish in the world, prized for its rich flavor and succulently flaky flesh. But while it's undeniably delicious, there can be some nuances in how sustainable certain varieties are. Sourcing sustainable alternatives can be tricky, but knowing the right certifications and sources can go a long way toward purchasing the right seafood.

Salmon isn't inherently unsustainable, but an incredible amount of global demand can lead to some less-than-ideal practices. In particular, open-net salmon farms may cause environmental issues, whether that's pollution runoff, unsustainable sources of fish feed, or the spread of diseases and parasites to wild populations. One of the biggest differences between farmed and wild salmon is that wild varieties are often more sustainable, depending on the fishery, and well-managed populations are carefully monitored to ensure long-term viability. Still, New Zealand is famous for its highly rated salmon aquaculture, so it would be wrong to paint all farms with the same brush.

When it comes to sourcing other, more sustainable fish, it's often a solid idea to look for something small and fast-growing rather than something large and predatory. While some certifications may greenwash the sustainability of seafood, guidance from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration can help consumers identify responsibly managed fisheries. Despite salmon's unique qualities, there are many fish out there that are more affordable and sustainable and can still be high-quality substitutes in your regular diet.

If you don't want to change up textures and taste, char can be a more sustainable fish with a mild flavor and fewer calories. As a salmonid, it's remarkably similar to salmon and has the same pink flesh, marbling, and savory skin you've already come to love.

Few fish species are quite as environmentally friendly as responsibly sourced sardines, since they're small prey fish that grow quite rapidly in their first years of life. Fresh, dried, frozen, or tinned, sardines come in enough varieties that there's an option for just about everyone.

Freshwater fish get a bad rap for being milder and leaner than ocean-dwelling species, and responsibly farmed rainbow trout is about as tasty and environmentally friendly as it gets. A thick, skin-on fillet cooked with a pat of butter can be just as moist and succulent, and modern farming practices can be quite eco-conscious.

Tasting like someone managed to cross the buttery sweetness of lobster with a fish, sablefish, also known as black cod, is an ocean delicacy. Even well-managed farming operations can have a relatively low environmental impact, particularly when they use responsible feed sources and strict measures to prevent disease.

Essentially just a giant perch, barramundi is a flaky, versatile protein you can prepare exactly the same way you'd cook salmon. They're a unique case in that they're quite large but can thrive on feeds containing plant-based ingredients, so responsibly managed commercial farming operations can have a relatively low environmental impact.

A catfish may not be much to look at, but they're certainly a lot to taste. As bottom-feeders, they can thrive on an omnivorous diet that includes plant-based ingredients, and while they might be a touch lean, few proteins are quite as good when deep-fried or bathed in butter.

One of the mildest fish you can use in just about anything, halibut is a largely sustainable choice, particularly when it's wild-caught in the Pacific. Atlantic populations have faced steep declines from overfishing, so be sure to source it appropriately.

When you're looking for something to bread, batter, or mix into a salad, few types of seafood are quite as good as whiting. Like other fish, however, its sustainability depends on its source, and some well-managed fisheries in U.S. Atlantic waters are more sustainable than those targeting depleted populations elsewhere.

While mahi-mahi sourced from Central America and southern Asia can be a bit problematic, those caught in responsibly managed fisheries in the Atlantic can be quite sustainable. While the fish can reach a respectable 3 feet in length, they grow rapidly, and their populations can recover quite quickly with responsible management.

Snapper is incredibly delicious, but of all the various species, yellowtail snapper from well-managed fisheries can be a particularly responsible choice. Historically, government authorities and local fishers work together to manage certain populations, helping ensure that these fish are harvested responsibly.

Huge, sweet, and oh-so-fun to reel in, the greater amberjack is a common sight for saltwater fishers looking to make tacos or cut thick steaks for the grill. Strict controls over harvesting wild-caught fish can help protect vulnerable populations, although sustainability varies by fishery, so it's worth checking the source before buying it at a seafood counter.

Sometimes called sunshine bass, this hybrid fish is a cross between a saltwater striped bass and a freshwater white bass. These fish grow quickly and tolerate a wide range of conditions, making it relatively easy to raise them sustainably with minimal environmental impact.

Eating carp can not only be sustainable, but buying invasive varieties sourced from the American South can actually be a boon for the environment! Several species of invasive carp have spread through U.S. waterways, so every bite of their earthy, slightly tangy flesh can help support efforts to protect these delicate ecosystems.

Blackened red drum, also called redfish, was once so popular that it prompted an outright commercial fishing ban in federal waters of the Gulf of Mexico. While responsibly farm-raised red drum can still be a sustainable choice, along with certain wild-caught black drum, it's generally still best to avoid wild-caught red drum, as sustainability varies by fishery.

Fresh, clean, and a premium delicacy, grouper can be a gray area of sustainability. While many species, like goliath, Nassau, and Gulf groupers, face serious conservation concerns and may be illegal to harvest in certain areas, responsibly sourced black grouper can be a great substitute for premium-grade salmon.

November has arrived, and while it's still fall and the time to enjoy the flavors of the season, retailers and consumers alike are gearing up for the holidays, beginning with Thanksgiving and continuing on to Christmas, Hanukkah, and other celebrations. As such, shelves at your favorite stores are being cleared of Halloween decorations and bags of trick-or-treat candy in favor of cornucopia motifs, pumpkin pies (some of which we've ranked), and turkeys. You may also begin to see Christmas trees, ornaments, and gift sets appear to inspire customers' holiday gift-giving.

The popular warehouse club is known for offering great value on bulk items, including multipacks of many popular brands. It also has many exclusive items that you may be hard-pressed to find at other stores, and you can now find an ever-increasing array of international products, too, along with items from its in-house Kirkland Signature brand. Below are our picks for some of the most noteworthy items available in November. whereas the Premium version offers a lot more functionality, it detects plagiarism in your content, suggests word choice, or adds fluency to it.

ProWritingAid can be used as an add-on to WordPress, Gmail, and Google Docs. The software also offers helpful articles, videos, quizzes, and explanations to help improve your writing.

Sounds like you're biased for Grammarly. Not really that informative if you're already leaning towards one to begin with. Still, it was an interesting read. Tell me, do you use Grammarly with your day-to-day writing/blogging?

I use the paid versions of both Grammarly and Pro Writing Aid. Both of them have issues:- Grammarly IS more focused on nonfiction than fiction. If you're writing fiction, you may find Grammarly's insistence on "Conciseness" annoying. They seem to want to take the soul out of your writing, which is fine for a corporate report or technical manual, but not for your Great American Novel.- Grammarly pushes features on users that are not ready for prime time. It doesn't matter that you never agreed to be a beta tester for them; you get to do it anyway.- Pro Writing Aid actually counts the occurrences of words in your document and tells you when a word has been overused compared to published literature. Grammarly, on the other hand, seems hell-bent to remove certain words that it has deemed overused from the language, whether or not they're actually overused in your document.- Grammarly's Clarity function is simply horrible. It mangles sentences and changes their meaning. Sometimes the result of its suggestion is unintelligible garbage.- Grammarly allows you to turn off some checks, but not all of them. Unfortunately, the ones you cannot turn off are some of the most irritating (such as that horrible "Clarity"). On the other hand, Pro Writing Aid lets you choose which checks you use.- Pro Writing Aid has a mediocre command of American English (it's a British product). The app insists on rules of grammar and spelling that are outright wrong, per Merriam-Webster, the Chicago Manual of Style, and modern usage as shown by Google Books Ngram. At one point, Pro Writing Aid insisted that American English did not include the words "holiday" and "autumn," that "vacation" and "fall" must be used instead.- Pro Writing Aid's rules for commas are 100 percent consistent with the way I learned them in high school--50 years ago! They do not reflect modern usage. Grammarly is much better at this.- Pro Writing Aid seems to waste their limited resources on tweaking their UI. Their UI most definitely could use improvement, but these changes are not great improvements; they only serve to confuse users. Their resources would be better spent fixing the many functional problems in their app.- Some of Pro Writing Aid's checks are completely useless, as they do not take context into consideration. For example, an ordinary word would not be capitalized as part of a narrative, but would be as part of a title (for example, "professor." But if you capitalize correctly for context, Pro Writing Aid dings you for "Inconsistent capitalization." Similar issues exist with hyphenation consistency check.Each of these applications has its strengths as well as considerable weaknesses. I will say that both of them are light-years better than the execrable grammar checker in Microsoft Word, but that's damning with faint praise.

#9817. Skip The McDonald's Egg McMuffin: The Fast Food Breakfast Sandwich With Thick, Crispy Bacon

When it comes to fast food breakfast sandwiches, McDonald's remains uppermost in many people's minds. And why not? The iconic Egg McMuffin, with its famously round egg patty, has been the cornerstone of the chain's breakfast menu since the 1970s. And while you can sub the Canadian bacon that comes standard on the McMuffin for regular bacon, Wendy's Breakfast Baconator actually takes the pork product to a whole new level if that's your sandwich protein preference. And more than that, it ranks as one of the best overall fast food breakfast sandwiches, based on the opinions of the customers who eat them.

Wendy's, which has only served breakfast nationwide on a permanent basis since 2020, is doing the morning meat right with its Breakfast Baconator, which features not only six strips of thick, crispy applewood-smoked bacon, but also a sausage patty — which, like the burgers, comes in a square shape — a freshly cracked egg cooked into a patty (Wendy's is one of the rare fast food chains that use real, whole eggs), two slices of American cheese, and a Swiss cheese sauce. Then, everything gets piled onto not a breakfast bread, like a bagel or English muffin, but a potato roll, which is perhaps better suited to hold the hefty fillings. This symphony of flavors and textures led one user on Reddit to call the immensely bacon-forward sandwich "peak fast food breakfast" that "simply just [can't] get any better," a sentiment echoed by plenty of fellow fans.

The Breakfast Baconator is pretty beloved as-is, but there are ways to modify the menu item and make it that much more enjoyable. One Redditor had the idea of actually stuffing more into the sandwich by adding Wendy's seasoned potato wedges and a flavorful sauce, writing that "it'll change your life." We think the Scorchin' Hot sauce would be an especially tasty addition.

Further, if the potato bun is too lunch-y for you, you can swap it out for a breakfast bread — try asking for the Breakfast Baconator on a biscuit. It's a modification that cannot be made on the app or online, so you'll have to verbally request the change when you place your order at the drive-thru or the counter, if your location still offers that option. Of course, if there simply isn't enough of something on the Breakfast Baconator for your tastes, you can add up to four more sausage patties, four more eggs, and extra Swiss cheese sauce.

#9813. What is Blockchain: Everything You Need to Know (2022)

Imagine a world in which you can do transactions and many other things without having to give your personal information. A world in which you don’t need to rely on banks or governments anymore. Sounds amazing, right? That’s exactly what blockchain technology allows us to do.

It’s like your computer’s hard drive. blockchain is a technology that lets you store data in digital blocks, which are connected together like links in a chain.

Blockchain technology was originally invented in 1991 by two mathematicians, Stuart Haber and W. Scot Stornetta. They first proposed the system to ensure that timestamps could not be tampered with.

A few years later, in 1998, software developer Nick Szabo proposed using a similar kind of technology to secure a digital payments system he called “Bit Gold.” However, this innovation was not adopted until Satoshi Nakamoto claimed to have invented the first Blockchain and Bitcoin.

A blockchain is a distributed database shared between the nodes of a computer network. It saves information in digital format. Many people first heard of blockchain technology when they started to look up information about bitcoin.

Blockchain is used in cryptocurrency systems to ensure secure, decentralized records of transactions.

Blockchain allowed people to guarantee the fidelity and security of a record of data without the need for a third party to ensure accuracy.

To understand how a blockchain works, Consider these basic steps:

Let’s get to know more about the blockchain.

Blockchain records digital information and distributes it across the network without changing it. The information is distributed among many users and stored in an immutable, permanent ledger that can't be changed or destroyed. That's why blockchain is also called "Distributed Ledger Technology" or DLT.

And that’s the beauty of it! The process may seem complicated, but it’s done in minutes with modern technology. And because technology is advancing rapidly, I expect things to move even more quickly than ever.

Even though blockchain is integral to cryptocurrency, it has other applications. For example, blockchain can be used for storing reliable data about transactions. Many people confuse blockchain with cryptocurrencies like bitcoin and ethereum.

Blockchain already being adopted by some big-name companies, such as Walmart, AIG, Siemens, Pfizer, and Unilever. For example, IBM's Food Trust uses blockchain to track food's journey before reaching its final destination.

Although some of you may consider this practice excessive, food suppliers and manufacturers adhere to the policy of tracing their products because bacteria such as E. coli and Salmonella have been found in packaged foods. In addition, there have been isolated cases where dangerous allergens such as peanuts have accidentally been introduced into certain products.

Tracing and identifying the sources of an outbreak is a challenging task that can take months or years. Thanks to the Blockchain, however, companies now know exactly where their food has been—so they can trace its location and prevent future outbreaks.

Blockchain technology allows systems to react much faster in the event of a hazard. It also has many other uses in the modern world.

Blockchain technology is safe, even if it’s public. People can access the technology using an internet connection.

Have you ever been in a situation where you had all your data stored at one place and that one secure place got compromised? Wouldn't it be great if there was a way to prevent your data from leaking out even when the security of your storage systems is compromised?

Blockchain technology provides a way of avoiding this situation by using multiple computers at different locations to store information about transactions. If one computer experiences problems with a transaction, it will not affect the other nodes.

Instead, other nodes will use the correct information to cross-reference your incorrect node. This is called “Decentralization,” meaning all the information is stored in multiple places.

Blockchain guarantees your data's authenticity—not just its accuracy, but also its irreversibility. It can also be used to store data that are difficult to register, like legal contracts, state identifications, or a company's product inventory.

Blockchain has many advantages and disadvantages.

I’ll answer the most frequently asked questions about blockchain in this section.

Blockchain is not a cryptocurrency but a technology that makes cryptocurrencies possible. It's a digital ledger that records every transaction seamlessly.

Yes, blockchain can be theoretically hacked, but it is a complicated task to be achieved. A network of users constantly reviews it, which makes hacking the blockchain difficult.

Coinbase Global is currently the biggest blockchain company in the world. The company runs a commendable infrastructure, services, and technology for the digital currency economy.

Blockchain is a decentralized technology. It’s a chain of distributed ledgers connected with nodes. Each node can be any electronic device. Thus, one owns blockhain.

Bitcoin is a cryptocurrency, which is powered by Blockchain technology while Blockchain is a distributed ledger of cryptocurrency

Generally a database is a collection of data which can be stored and organized using a database management system. The people who have access to the database can view or edit the information stored there. The client-server network architecture is used to implement databases. whereas a blockchain is a growing list of records, called blocks, stored in a distributed system. Each block contains a cryptographic hash of the previous block, timestamp and transaction information. Modification of data is not allowed due to the design of the blockchain. The technology allows decentralized control and eliminates risks of data modification by other parties.

Blockchain has a wide spectrum of applications and, over the next 5-10 years, we will likely see it being integrated into all sorts of industries. From finance to healthcare, blockchain could revolutionize the way we store and share data. Although there is some hesitation to adopt blockchain systems right now, that won't be the case in 2022-2023 (and even less so in 2026). Once people become more comfortable with the technology and understand how it can work for them, owners, CEOs and entrepreneurs alike will be quick to leverage blockchain technology for their own gain. #9810. Give Scrambled Eggs An Instant Flavor Boost With A Packet You Have In The Pantry

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

When you want an easy breakfast, eggs are key to a protein-rich morning meal that can be made in minutes — but for maximum flavor, you might want to think about scrambling them because you can mix them with any spice, herb, or seasoning you'd like. For example, pairing taco seasoning with your scrambled eggs creates an incomparable taste that requires only a few seconds of extra work.

For the simplest preparation, you can just whisk a teaspoon of the seasoning — we like McCormick Original Taco Seasoning Mix, available on Amazon — to about six eggs before you cook them, which will feed two to three people for breakfast. Most premade taco seasoning mixes contain plenty of salt, plus cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, and other spices, so you may be ready to go right out of the packet without needing to add anything else. But you can customize it to get exactly the flavor profile you're looking for.

If you're eating the eggs right off the plate, think about adding some cheese — Monterey Jack melts beautifully, and you can add a little extra spice with pepper jack. But cheddar is always a good choice and can add a sharper flavor, depending on what you use. For more creaminess, try Havarti, or go for Comté for some nutty undertones. From there, some freshly chopped cilantro or a drizzle of hot sauce makes for delicious toppings.

If you want to make a whole meal, you can add some extra ingredients to your plate. Putting a little chorizo in your scrambled eggs will give them a richer, spicier flavor, plus more protein. Or think about making summery breakfast tacos or burritos. You can cook sauteed onions, potatoes, and bell peppers, then mix it all together with your spiced eggs. All you need to do is wrap the mixture in your favorite tortilla, and you can enjoy it at the breakfast table or on the go.

#9809. Is a gas oven bad for bread?: Why a gas oven may be interfering with your go-to steaming method.

Adapted from King Arthur Baking Company’s Big Book of Bread

One of the most crucial steps for making crusty artisan-style bread comes at the very end: steaming.

Baking bread with steam is critical for achieving expansive, open-crumbed loaves with a golden, crisp crust. If you bake bread in a dry oven, the crust quickly sets, which prevents the dough from expanding to its full potential; this, in turn, leads to loaves with a denser crumb. If you introduce steam at the start of the bake, the crust remains moist and pliable and the loaf can stretch and expand before the crust sets, resulting in a lighter, more open crumb.

What’s more, steam also helps gelatinize starches on the loaf’s exterior, which helps it brown and creates an especially crispy, flavorful, and shiny loaf. (Learn more: A guide to baking bread with steam at home.)

There are many different ways to steam your bread, all of which are designed to introduce moisture to the oven during the first part of baking. The most common method involves setting a large cast-iron skillet below your baking stone or steel when you preheat the oven. After you load your bread into the oven, you immediately pour a cup or so of warm water into the preheated cast-iron skillet and quickly close the door so the steam doesn’t escape.

This method works great, with one exception: It’s not effective in a gas oven.

If you have a gas oven, it’s very hard to add sufficient steam. By design, gas ovens vent out effluence, meaning whatever steam you add is very quickly vented out of the oven chamber. This is particularly true if you steam your bread by pouring hot water into a cast-iron skillet, as outlined above. All the water quickly dissipates, and there’s not enough moisture left to enhance the crust.

But all is not lost. There is a workaround.

If you’re steaming bread in a gas oven, you need to use a preheated covered baker, such as a Dutch oven. Instead of adding an additional water source, the lidded vessel traps the steam that escapes from the loaf as it bakes, becoming a kind of self-steaming oven. Because the steam is sealed in, the gas oven won’t vent it out.

You can use a Dutch oven for a round, boule-shaped loaf, or any other form of covered baker, like the Brod & Taylor Bread Steel for elongated, bâtard-shaped loaves. (There’s also a round version of the Bread Steel available.)

For more guidance on this method, see our previous blogs, Bread baking in a Dutch oven and For crispy, crackle crusts, put a lid on it.

When you load your dough into the oven, slip a few ice cubes between the parchment beneath your loaf and the pan to give the loaf an extra initial burst of steam. Just don’t skip the parchment beneath the dough. Otherwise, the extra water from the melting ice may cause your bread to stick to the pot.

#9807. Most Frequently Asked Questions About Affiliate Marketing

Affiliate marketing is a way to make money by promoting the products and services of other people and companies. You don't need to create your product or service, just promote existing ones. That's why it's so easy to get started with affiliate marketing. You can even get started with no budget at all!

An affiliate program is a package of information you create for your product, which is then made available to potential publishers. The program will typically include details about the product and its retail value, commission levels, and promotional materials. Many affiliate programs are managed via an affiliate network like ShareASale, which acts as a platform to connect publishers and advertisers, but it is also possible to offer your program directly.

Affiliate networks connect publishers to advertisers.  Affiliate networks make money by charging fees to the merchants who advertise with them; these merchants are known as advertisers. The percentage of each sale that the advertiser pays is negotiated between the merchant and the affiliate network.

Dropshipping is a method of selling that allows you to run an online store without having to stock products. You advertise the products as if you owned them, but when someone makes an order, you create a duplicate order with the distributor at a reduced price. The distributor takes care of the post and packaging on your behalf. As affiliate marketing is based on referrals and this type of drop shipping requires no investment in inventory when a customer buys through the affiliate link, no money exchanges hands.

Performance marketing is a method of marketing that pays for performance, like when a sale is made or an ad is clicked This can include methods like PPC (pay-per-click) or display advertising. Affiliate marketing is one form of performance marketing where commissions are paid out to affiliates on a performance basis when they click on their affiliate link and make a purchase or action.

Smartphones are essentially miniature computers, so publishers can display the same websites and offers that are available on a PC. But mobiles also offer specific tools not available on computers, and these can be used to good effect for publishers. Publishers can optimize their ads for mobile users by making them easy to access by this audience. Publishers can also make good use of text and instant messaging to promote their offers. As the mobile market is predicted to make up 80% of traffic in the future, publishers who do not promote on mobile devices are missing out on a big opportunity.

The best way to find affiliate publishers is on reputable networks like ShareASale Cj(Commission Junction), Awin, and Impact radius. These networks have a strict application process and compliance checks, which means that all affiliates are trustworthy.

An affiliate disclosure statement discloses to the reader that there may be affiliate links on a website, for which a commission may be paid to the publisher if visitors follow these links and make purchases.

Publishers promote their programs through a variety of means, including blogs, websites, email marketing, and pay-per-click ads. Social media has a huge interactive audience, making this platform a good source of potential traffic.

A super affiliate is an affiliate partner who consistently drives a large majority of sales from any program they promote, compared to other affiliate partners involved in that program.  Affiliates make a lot of money from affiliate marketing Pat Flynn earned more than $50000 in 2013 from affiliate marketing.

Because the Internet is so widespread, affiliate programs can be promoted in any country. Affiliate strategies that are set internationally need to be tailored to the language of the targeted country.

Affiliate marketing can help you grow your business in the following ways:

One of the best ways to work with qualified affiliates is to hire an affiliate marketing agency that works with all the networks. Affiliates are carefully selected and go through a rigorous application process to be included in the network.

Affiliate marketing is generally associated with websites, but there are other ways to promote your affiliate links, including:

To build your affiliate marketing business, you don't have to invest money in the beginning. You can sign up for free with any affiliate network and start promoting their brands right away.

Commission rates are typically based on a percentage of the total sale and in some cases can also be a flat fee for each transaction. The rates are set by the merchant.

Some merchants run their affiliate programs internally, while others choose to contract out management to a network or an external agency.

#9804. TOP 11 AI MARKETING TOOLS YOU SHOULD USE (Updated 2022)

If you’re late to the AI party, don’t worry. It’s easier than you think to start leveraging artificial intelligence tools in your marketing strategy. Here are 11 AI marketing tools every marketer should start using today.

Personalize is an AI-powered technology that helps you identify and produce highly targeted sales and marketing campaigns by tracking the products and services your contacts are most interested in at any given time. The platform uses an algorithm to identify each contact’s top three interests, which are updated in real-time based on recent site activity.

Seventh Sense provides behavioral analytics that helps you win attention in your customers’ overcrowded email inboxes. Choosing the best day and time to send an email is always a gamble. And while some days of the week generally get higher open rates than others, you’ll never be able to nail down a time that’s best for every customer. Seventh Sense eases your stress of having to figure out the perfect send-time and day for your email campaigns. The AI-based platform figures out the best timing and email frequency for each contact based on when they’re opening emails. The tool is primarily geared toward HubSpot and Marketo customers

Phrasee uses artificial intelligence to help you write more effective subject lines. With its AI-based Natural Language Generation system, Phrasee uses data-driven insights to generate millions of natural-sounding copy variants that match your brand voice. The model is end-to-end, meaning when you feed the results back to Phrasee, the prediction model rebuilds so it can continuously learn from your audience.

HubSpot Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is an integral tool for the Human Content team. It uses machine learning to determine how search engines understand and categorize your content. HubSpot SEO helps you improve your search engine rankings and outrank your competitors. Search engines reward websites that organize their content around core subjects, or topic clusters. HubSpot SEO helps you discover and rank for the topics that matter to your business and customers.

When you’re limited to testing two variables against each other at a time, it can take months to get the results you’re looking for. Evolv AI lets you test all your ideas at once. It uses advanced algorithms to identify the top-performing concepts, combine them with each other, and repeat the process to achieve the best site experience.

Acrolinx is a content alignment platform that helps brands scale and improves the quality of their content. It’s geared toward enterprises – its major customers include big brands like Google, Adobe, and Amazon - to help them scale their writing efforts. Instead of spending time chasing down and fixing typos in multiple places throughout an article or blog post, you can use Acrolinx to do it all right there in one place. You start by setting your preferences for style, grammar, tone of voice, and company-specific word usage. Then, Acrolinx checks and scores your existing content to find what’s working and suggest areas for improvement. The platform provides real-time guidance and suggestions to make writing better and strengthen weak pages.

MarketMuse uses an algorithm to help marketers build content strategies. The tool shows you where to target keywords to rank in specific topic categories, and recommends keywords you should go after if you want to own particular topics. It also identifies gaps and opportunities for new content and prioritizes them by their probable impact on your rankings. The algorithm compares your content with thousands of articles related to the same topic to uncover what’s missing from your site.

Copilot is a suite of tools that help eCommerce businesses maintain real-time communication with customers around the clock at every stage of the funnel. Promote products, recover shopping carts and send updates or reminders directly through Messenger.

Yotpo’s deep learning technology evaluates your customers’ product reviews to help you make better business decisions. It identifies key topics that customers mention related to your products—and their feelings toward them. The AI engine extracts relevant reviews from past buyers and presents them in smart displays to convert new shoppers. Yotpo also saves you time moderating reviews. The AI-powered moderation tool automatically assigns a score to each review and flags reviews with negative sentiment so you can focus on quality control instead of manually reviewing every post.

Albert is a self-learning software that automates the creation of marketing campaigns for your brand. It analyzes vast amounts of data to run optimized campaigns autonomously, allowing you to feed in your own creative content and target markets, and then use data from its database to determine key characteristics of a serious buyer. Albert identifies potential customers that match those traits, and runs trial campaigns on a small group of customers—with results refined by Albert himself—before launching it on a larger scale.

Albert plugs into your existing marketing technology stack, so you still have access to your accounts, ads, search, social media, and more. Albert maps tracking and attribution to your source of truth so you can determine which channels are driving your business.

There are many tools and companies out there that offer AI tools, but this is a small list of resources that we have found to be helpful. If you have any other suggestions, feel free to share them in the comments below this article. As marketing evolves at such a rapid pace, new marketing strategies will be invented that we haven't even dreamed of yet. But for now, this list should give you a good starting point on your way to implementing AI into your marketing mix.

#9803. Taming Autonomous AI Agents with Rootless Docker

Senior DevOps/Platform Engineer, ~15 years in DevOps, platform engineering & AEM. Deep AWS, Kubernetes/EKS, cloud-native expertise.

Senior DevOps/Platform Engineer, ~15 years in DevOps, platform engineering & AEM. Deep AWS, Kubernetes/EKS, cloud-native expertise.

Senior DevOps/Platform Engineer, ~15 years in DevOps, platform engineering & AEM. Deep AWS, Kubernetes/EKS, cloud-native expertise.

Autonomous coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Cline and their MCP-wired cousins ask before running shell commands by default, but that gate erodes fast in practice. Developers allowlist docker once, switch on auto-approve for long tasks, or wire an MCP server that calls the Engine API directly with no prompt at all. When agents inherit a Docker CLI pointed at a rootful daemon, every docker run, docker exec and socket-mounted sidecar becomes a privileged execution path on the host. Rootless Docker, Linux user namespaces and cgroups v2 together form a containment layer for agent-driven container workloads, provided agents are wired to the right socket and can't fall back to the system daemon.

The Docker Engine API is root-equivalent. Any process that can open /var/run/docker.sock can create a privileged container, bind-mount the host filesystem, or escape through device nodes. Mounting the socket :ro doesn't change this. A read-only bind mount protects the socket file, not the HTTP requests sent through it.

Autonomous agents amplify that blast radius. A single prompt like "reproduce the CI failure in Docker" can cascade into:

The failure mode isn't a malicious operator. It's a probabilistic tool-caller with shell access and incomplete context. A "helpful" retry loop that re-pulls images, recreates networks and restarts Compose projects looks like routine automation in the transcript and like a change storm on the host. The defense has to be structural: demote the daemon itself, then put a quota on every container it creates.

Rootless Docker runs dockerd and containerd inside a user namespace created by RootlessKit. Every request an agent makes crosses these layers:

Rootless mode depends on subordinate ID ranges in /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid:

RootlessKit builds the namespace's ID map from two sources. Container UID 0 maps to the invoking user's own host UID, for example 1001 for deploy. Container UIDs 1 through 65536 map to the subordinate range, so container UID 1 is host UID 100000, and so on.

Root inside a container is therefore never root on the host. A process that escapes a container holds the deploying user's privileges, and files that container root creates on bind mounts are owned by that user. The rule that follows: run agent workloads under a dedicated, low-privilege service account, never a developer's personal login, so that "the user's privileges" means almost nothing.

dockerd-rootless.sh starts the daemon under rootlesskit, which creates the namespaces, applies the ID mapping through the setuid helpers newuidmap and newgidmap, and starts the networking helper.

Rootful Docker attaches containers to a host bridge (docker0) and programs host iptables as real root. Rootless Docker can't. Its network lives inside RootlessKit's own namespace, connected to the host by a user-mode network stack. That's slirp4netns when installed, and otherwise gvisor-tap-vsock; pasta is available experimentally. Container traffic leaves the host as ordinary sockets owned by the unprivileged user.

Containers egress as the deploying user, not as the host's packet-filter authority. Host firewall policy is therefore a separate concern: don't assume egress restrictions you never configured.

User namespaces stop privilege escalation; cgroups v2 stops resource exhaustion. Rootless Docker applies cgroup limits only when running with cgroup v2 and systemd. In that case, docker info reports Cgroup Driver: systemd. If it reports none, rootless Docker silently ignores --memory, --cpus and --pids-limit.

Even with systemd, the user's slice typically receives only the memory and pids controllers. cpu and io limits require extra delegation, configured system-wide in section 6.

Disk saturation from image pulls and builds

Every agent-launched container should carry explicit limits:

Setting --memory-swap equal to --memory disables extra swap. --pids-limit is non-negotiable for agents that spawn shells and package managers. --cpus sets a hard cpu.max quota, while --cpu-shares is only a relative weight under contention.

Verify that the CPU controller, the one that usually isn't delegated, actually works:

You should see 50000 100000. If the command fails or the limit is missing, cpu isn't delegated to your user. Apply the drop-in in section 6 before blaming the agent wrapper.

Most agent configurations and MCP servers default to /var/run/docker.sock, the rootful system socket. Rootless Docker listens elsewhere:

If DOCKER_HOST is unset and the client falls back to the system socket, every rootless boundary you built is bypassed. Agents running as systemd user units, IDE extensions or MCP child processes often inherit a minimal environment that lacks XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.

A resolution order that holds up in production:

Wrappers and MCP servers should stat the runtime path before connecting. Pair that with a deny rule if the socket's peer credentials (SO_PEERCRED) show UID 0 when the agent expected a user daemon. IDE-spawned children usually inherit HOME but not XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. Setting DOCKER_HOST explicitly in the MCP server definition matters as much as the rootless install itself.

None (rules stay inside RootlessKit's namespace)

Capabilities apply only inside the user namespace

Requires systemd driver; cpu/io need delegation

Blocked without sysctl or capability changes

Rootless isn't a substitute for an application-level policy proxy. It's the execution substrate that makes a compromised or confused agent survivable. Keep the MCP tool surface narrow, and use rootless Docker so whatever still reaches the Engine API can't trivially become host root.

Containers can't gain privileges through setuid binaries

Each container sees only its own cgroup tree

Lets RootlessKit's port driver propagate client source IPs

Process limits belong in cgroups through --pids-limit, not in an nproc ulimit. Under user namespaces, nproc counts processes per host UID, so containers would share one budget with each other and with the daemon.

Delegation is configured on the system's user@.service, not on the user's Docker unit, and needs root:

/etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/delegate.conf:

The output should list cpu io memory pids. Add cpuset to the Delegate= line, which requires systemd 244 or later, if agents need --cpuset-cpus.

After dockerd-rootless-setuptool.sh install, cap the daemon itself:

~/.config/systemd/user/docker.service.d/override.conf:

These limits apply to the daemon's own processes: dockerd, containerd, RootlessKit and the network helper. Containers get their own systemd scopes, limited per container.

Don't add NoNewPrivileges=true to this unit. RootlessKit needs the setuid helpers newuidmap and newgidmap to build the ID mapping, and NoNewPrivileges stops them from gaining privileges, so the daemon fails to start. Clients choose the socket through DOCKER_HOST, so setting it in this unit has no effect.

--network none is the right starting point for build and test agents that don't need egress. Open networking only when the task requires it. Dropping all capabilities and running as nobody closes the obvious privilege ladders even inside the user namespace.

Rootless dockerd, subordinate ID mappings, user-mode networking and cgroups v2 quotas turn agent container access from an implicit root grant into a bounded, observable workload. The remaining gap is the agent's client side. An MCP server that still resolves /var/run/docker.sock quietly undoes all of it.

docker-mcp-guardian is an open-source MCP server that gives Claude and similar agents read-mostly access to Docker. It's read-only by default, resolves restart deny-lists by canonical container name, withholds secrets from inspect output, and bounds every daemon call with a timeout. It also implements the resolution order from section 4: an explicit DOCKER_HOST, then the rootless socket, and the rootful socket only with GUARDIAN_ALLOW_ROOTFUL=true. With no acceptable endpoint it fails closed instead of connecting.

Two open issues take rootless support further, and contributions are welcome:

Pick one, point your own agents at a rootless socket, and help make safe container access the default for autonomous coding tools.

#9802. No Beer, No Problem: Add A Splash Of This Drink For The Crunchiest Onion Rings

A top-tier onion ring brings together several textural qualities into one bite. You want enough heft to encase the slivers of allium, yet a crunchy consistency that's delicate. Each bite should contain both onion and batter, and while seasoning should be present, the onion's internal sweetness should still come through. It's a complex balance to get right, with beer often used as a cornerstone of the batter.

The beverage lends several advantages to onion rings: The hops and malt add flavor, the alcohol evaporates quickly during frying, and — most importantly — the carbonation creates an airy batter that translates to crunchiness. However, if you're not keen on adding a brew to your onion ring recipe, no fear: Sparkling water is a terrific alternative. Just like beer, the carbonation works its textural magic. And when used alongside rice flour (a tempura influence), you'll produce some of the crispiest onion rings, with an even more delicate texture.

It's critical to pour the sparkling water in as cold as possible — temperature control is essential for optimal crispness. As a result, you'll want to incorporate the water right out of the fridge, at the conclusion of batter preparation. Stir until the batter is homogeneous and on the liquidy side, similar to pancake or waffle batter in consistency. And you can also dredge the onions in flour separately first to make sure the breading sticks. Put the two elements together, deep-fry, and you'll get an onion ring rendition that is no less successful than a beer-based one.

Unlike beer and other flavored carbonated beverages, sparkling water's neutral flavor can be used to your advantage. Such a batter comes out lighter and without much added flavor, letting you tweak the seasonings to your liking. A rendition can be kept to a straightforward salt-only seasoning, which really puts the onions front and center. Or you can go with more flavorful spices like onion and garlic powder, paprika, and a dash of cayenne for heat. Don't rule out using some dried herbs in the batter, either; parsley flakes lend a nice herbal touch, for example. Apply seasoning both to the batter and after cooking to ensure comprehensive flavoring.

Want to up the crisp even further? Reach for some starchy ingredients other than flour and cornstarch. Dry potato flakes will lend your onion rings a pleasant starchy spin, and for an extra-golden-brown character, coat the dish with panko. Without beer in the mix, you can still achieve a light, airy texture. Serve them alongside homemade ranch, and it's an onion ring composition you'll want to make again and again.

#9798. Add Cowboy Candy To Your Next Grilled Cheese For Triple The Flavor

Making the best grilled cheese can be serious business. And though the modern grilled cheese didn't take off until the 1920s — when commercially sliced bread and process cheese made it an affordable household staple — one perfect add-on for your next sandwich carries a classic frontier spirit. It's called cowboy candy — sugared and pickled jalapeño peppers — and each slice adds an incredible amount of flavor to your meal.

If you like the sweet and sour mix of bread and butter pickles, and you can handle a decent hit of spiciness, you'll love cowboy candy. When jalapeños are pickled, the brine can mellow their heat, so you won't just get a blast of intense spiciness. You'll get crunchy, vegetal, and herbaceous notes; some nice tang from the vinegar; plus a hit of sweetness. And it goes with just about any cheese you want to put on your sando. Cheddar or Monterey Jack are classic American options. If you want more nuttiness, you can try Gruyère, or give Havarti a go for some nice buttery flavor that would also be delicious with caramelized onions. And adding some spicy chorizo will make it a full meal.

The history of cowboy candy begins in the Lone Star State. WHH Ranch, which is based in Texas, claims to be the originator of the condiment and the oldest family-owned cannery in the state. These days, you can order a variety of cowboy candy versions from its website.

If you want to make cowboy candy at home, it's not hard to do on your own. You're going to need a mix of sugar, vinegar, and pickling spices. The mixture will cook down into a thick syrup to give the peppers a nice sugary coating that turns a regular spicy grilled cheese into a masterful mix of flavors. For the spices, you can go the standard route with mustard seeds, celery seeds, and turmeric for the tasty bread and butter pickle style. But a little dried or fresh dill will get you closer to a classic dill pickle flavor, and some chipotle pepper powder will add more smokiness. If you want more of a pungent tang, you can add some apple cider vinegar.

When you're making your cowboy candy grilled cheese, think about what cheeses will blend best with the sweet, spicy, savory flavor. Maybe try a nice sourdough or thick Texas toast, and don't be afraid to try some other protein additions. Turn it into a taco-inspired sandwich with some seasoned ground beef, or use up the leftovers from your rotisserie chicken. Just get that cowboy candy for your next grilled cheese, and from there, you can pile on the flavor.

#9795. This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon.

As fall baking season settles in, you're probably reaching for apples — and the many flavor-packed ingredients they produce. Applesauce cooks down into tangy apple butter to be cradled in a flaky galette, while a drop of boiled cider can deliver supercharged apple flavor to crumb cake. But the baking ingredient you may be overlooking may be something you associate more with salad dressings and wellness tonics: apple cider vinegar.

This tangy, apple-y vinegar is a secret ingredient in some of our favorite fall recipes, including cookbook author Claire Saffitz’s Cinnamon-and-Sugar Apple Pie. While lemon juice is the standard acid used in most fruit pie fillings, Claire opts for apple cider vinegar here to complement the filling’s flavors. “It helps as a flavor enhancer, and I also like that it’s apple cider in an apple pie. It’s a nice symmetry,” she mentions.

Similarly, apple cider vinegar is used in the cooking liquid alongside sugar and butter to caramelize apples in a Classic Apple Tarte Tatin. The benefit is twofold: Vinegar’s acidity helps cut the sweetness of the caramel, and it prevents the apples from getting too mushy, instead maintaining their fork-tender texture.

Pastry chef and cookbook author Natasha Pickowicz often leans into the jolt vinegar can add, including adding a few drops to her cake soaks for an additional layer of flavor. “Cake soaks should have a balance of tart, sweet, and savory notes — just like vinaigrette for your favorite salad,” she writes in her cookbook More Than Cake. It can add intrigue to layered cakes like this Golden Spice Cake or Pumpkin Layer Cake. In her cookbook, she also calls for a glaze spiked with apple cider vinegar to brush onto an apple tart after baking. It’s the finishing touch “to further emphasize the tart’s resolute apple-ness,” she writes.

Apple cider vinegar doesn’t need to be limited to only apple desserts, either. In our Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, we call for apple cider vinegar as a foil to the brown sugar filling’s cloying sweetness. A spoonful of apple cider vinegar may not announce itself boldly, but it makes a small splash for brighter, more balanced bakes.
